title: How to Write a Git Commit Message
author: Chris Beams
version: 2014-08-31; the address is the publisher's and was not fetched in this container

record.source: Seven rules: separate the subject from the body with a blank line, limit the subject to 50 characters, capitalise it, end it without a period, use the imperative mood, wrap the body at 72, and use the body to explain what and why rather than how.
record.kept: The blank line, the imperative subject, and the body carrying the reason.
record.rewritten: The 50 and 72 become the budgets the ADR adjudicates; capitalisation and the no-period rule are not adopted, because the subject begins with a lower-case type prefix.
record.added: The type prefix, the machine check over the message, and the delivery/intermediate split.
record.dropped: Capitalisation, the trailing-period rule, and the rule against wrapping the body, which this repository states as a paragraph budget instead.
